title: HTTP Event Bridge: graceful rejoin protocol, semantic segmentation, and function-call boundary guarantees
creator: Ava Chen
description: Implement an HTTP Event Stream (EventSource/SSE) bridge that provides graceful reconnect and semantic segmentation for streaming LLM responses. The goal is to ensure tool/function-call boundaries and structured (JSON/JSONL) outputs remain parseable after client reconnects or transient network loss. This ticket covers protocol design, wire framing (length-prefixed segments + semantic markers), resume handshake, server-side checkpointing, and a compatibility shim for older SDKs that only understand naive line-delimited chunks.
acceptance_criteria: Clients can reconnect and resume a stream without losing function-call atomicity for in-flight tool invocations
Server emits segment metadata (segment_id, seq, checksum, semantic_tag) per framed unit; client can detect missing segments and request backfill or safe truncation

Backward-compatible behavior: legacy clients that expect plain JSONL continue to receive concatenated JSONL with a safe prefix heuristic; new clients can opt into the richer resume handshake via X-Stream-Protocol header
End-to-end tests exercising reconnect at: token boundary, JSON token mid-structure, function-call boundaries, and after a multi-segment backfill
Observability: traces include resume_token issuance and segment-level delivery latency; Console dashboard shows resume rate and backfill counts per model-route
tasks: Draft protocol spec (HTTP headers, per-segment envelope, resume handshake) and link to design doc
Implement server-side segmenter that emits length-prefixed frames with semantic_tag (e.g., 'text', 'function_call', 'tool_output', 'meta')
Build lightweight resume token generator tied to idempotent session + offset; persist short-lived resume tokens for configurable lease window
Add compatibility shim: when client omits X-Stream-Protocol, fallback to line-delimited JSONL and insert safe boundary markers as comments
Update SDKs: JS and Python opt-in to new handshake, expose onReconnect hooks and reassembly helpers
Create chaos tests: drop connection at random byte offsets and verify application-level semantics
Add Console metrics: resume_attempts, resume_success_rate, backfill_bytes, avg_backfill_latency
decisions: Use length-prefixed frames (32-bit little-endian) rather than newline delimiters to avoid ambiguity with JSON payloads
Semantic tags will be small enum strings to allow clients to apply different reassembly strategies (e.g., always replay 'meta', re-request 'tool_output' on checksum mismatch)
Resume tokens are lease-based and opaque; server validates session affinity + offset and returns a canonical resume_offset to start replay
To maintain low-latency, server will stream backfill concurrently with catch-up delivery and then switch to live token stream once caught up
Compatibility mode will include a best-effort boundary comment ('//SEGMENT-START id=...') that legacy clients will ignore but helps human debugging
risks: Clients that ignore semantic semantics could see duplicate tool invocations if they re-trigger retries; mitigation: server-side idempotency tokens for tool calls
Lease-based resume tokens require clock/invalidation tuning; misconfiguration may allow stale tokens or too-short windows causing poor UX
Length-prefixed frames increase parsing complexity for very small clients or proxies that expect newline-delimited SSE events
Backfill can amplify load spikes when many clients reconnect simultaneously; we need throttling/queueing policy
